2027-01-11.title: Monday after the First Sunday after Denho · Mar Gregorios of Nyssa
readings: He gives the Spirit without measure
2027-01-11.verse: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and the God of all consolation, who consoles us in all our affliction, so that we may be able to console those who are in any affliction with the consolation with which we ourselves are consoled by God.
theo: Paul opens his second letter to the Corinthians not with complaints about his sufferings, though they were many, but with a blessing: God is “the Father of mercies and the God of all consolation”. In Asia Paul had felt “the sentence of death”, and he learned to “rely not on ourselves but on God who raises the dead.” The comfort he received becomes comfort he can give. Our wounds, once consoled by God, become a ministry to others.

In the Gospel John the Baptist says of Jesus: “He whom God has sent speaks the words of God, for he gives the Spirit without measure.” Today we remember Mar Gregorios of Nyssa, younger brother of Mar Baselios, a bishop and mystic who taught that the soul never stops growing toward God: each discovery opens a greater longing. The Spirit given without measure keeps drawing us further into the endless love of God.

2027-01-11.prayer: Father of mercies and God of all consolation, you comfort us in every affliction. Teach us to rely on you who raise the dead, fill us with the Spirit without measure, and through the prayers of Mar Gregorios let us grow without end in your love. Amen.
altar: In the Holy Qurbono we receive the consolation of the risen Christ, so that we may carry it to those who suffer.

quick: God is the Father of mercies and God of all consolation.

2027-01-11.question: How can the comfort I received become comfort for someone else?

family.explain: St Paul says God comforts us when we are sad, so that we can comfort others who are sad.
family.intention: We pray for someone in our family or neighbourhood who is sad.
family.ask: Ask: “Who can we comfort this week?”

illus: A mother in Kollam who lost her son in an accident later joined a parish group visiting bereaved families. She says: I cannot take away their pain, but I can sit with them as someone who knows. God's comfort reached me so that it could reach them.

pm.open: Father of mercies, God of all consolation, comfort us as we gather, and make us comforters of others. Amen.
share: The God of all consolation (2 Corinthians 1:3). When have I felt God's comfort?
Rely not on ourselves but on God who raises the dead (2 Corinthians 1:9). Where must I trust more?
He gives the Spirit without measure (John 3:34). How do I make room for the Spirit?
interc: For those in grief and affliction.
For those who comfort others in hospitals and homes.
For bishops and theologians, through Mar Gregorios.
For those facing danger or death.
For our group, that we may grow in God's love.
pm.close: Father, you console us so that we may console others. Fill us with your Spirit and make us bearers of your comfort. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Paul had suffered greatly in Asia. He even felt he had received the sentence of death. Yet he begins his letter with a blessing: blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and the God of all consolation (2 Corinthians 1:3).
God consoles us in all our affliction, so that we may be able to console others with the consolation we ourselves have received. Our healed wounds become a ministry.
Paul says his trials taught him to rely not on ourselves but on God who raises the dead (2 Corinthians 1:9). Suffering strips away false supports and leaves us leaning on God alone.

Today we remember Mar Gregorios of Nyssa, brother of Mar Baselios, who taught that the soul is always growing toward God. Christ gives the Spirit without measure (John 3:34). Let us receive God's comfort, pass it on, and keep growing in his love. Amen.
kids: Children, when you are sad, God comforts you. Then you can comfort a friend who is sad. Who can you cheer up today?

intro: Theme: “The Father of mercies and the God of all consolation.”
Consoled to console; trusting the God who raises the dead.

q: Comfort, O comfort my people, says your God.

Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and the God of all consolation, who consoles us in all our affliction, so that we may be able to console those who are in any affliction with the consolation with which we ourselves are consoled by God.
points.apply: Comfort one suffering person this week.

points.h: Relying on God who raises the dead
q: For you have delivered my soul from death, my eyes from tears, my feet from stumbling.
Indeed, we felt that we had received the sentence of death so that we would rely not on ourselves but on God who raises the dead.
points.apply: Hand over one fear to God in prayer today.

q: Then the LORD came down in the cloud and spoke to him, and took some of the spirit that was on him and put it on the seventy elders; and when the spirit rested upon them, they prophesied. But they did not do so again.
He whom God has sent speaks the words of God, for he gives the Spirit without measure.
points.apply: Add five minutes to your daily prayer.

concl: God consoles us so that we may console.
With Mar Gregorios, let us keep growing in God.
